# Hydrilla AI: full text

Hydrilla AI is an AI 3D workspace for studio and artist pipelines. Generate 3D models from text or an image with BlueFox, Hydrilla's 3D model, check them in the browser, and work with Water Agent, the AI 3D agent for artists and studios.

Last updated: 2026-11-07

## Names
- Hydrilla AI is the product and company (serving studios and artists worldwide including the United States, India, Japan, China, and France); Hawan Research Labs is its research lab. https://hydrilla.ai/about
- Hawan Research Labs is Hydrilla AI's research lab, where the 3D research happens and BlueFox is built. https://hydrilla.ai/research
- BlueFox, Hydrilla's 3D model, is built by Hydrilla AI. Its current version is BlueFox 1, generally available to everyone in Hydrilla. https://hydrilla.ai/bluefox
- Hydrilla Water Agent is the AI 3D agent that works alongside artists and studios, from brief to finished assets, inside the tools they already use. https://hydrilla.ai/water
- Hydrilla here is the AI 3D company, not the aquatic plant.

## Key facts
- Plans (monthly, USD): Free $0 (100 credits), Starter $5 (900), Pro $12 (3,000, REST API access), Hourly $3 (900, one chosen hour a day), Hourly Pro $8 (3,000, chosen daily window; 33% off Pro). https://hydrilla.ai/pricing
- Credits don't roll over. At default quality, a model from text costs 45 credits and from an uploaded image 30.
- Start on the Free plan, or try any Monthly or Hourly plan, Pro included, free for 14 days. The trial needs a card.
- Every plan, Free included, exports every format. Formats: https://hydrilla.ai/features#exports
- Water Agent costs no credits and is included on every plan. It works in the Hydrilla app and inside Blender, Unity, Unreal, and Godot through the Hydrilla plugin.
- Hydrilla doesn't use customer data to train its models. https://hydrilla.ai/security
- Contact: founders@hydrilla.ai. Demos: https://cal.com/hydrilla

## Text to 3D with BlueFox

Describe an asset, approve a picture of it, and BlueFox, Hydrilla's 3D model, builds it as a segmented 3D model in Hydrilla AI. [About BlueFox](https://hydrilla.ai/bluefox)

### Four steps from prompt to model

Text to 3D starts with a reference image that you can refine before the 3D model is generated.

1. Write a prompt naming the subject, its style, and its use.
2. An image model renders a reference, at Low or High quality, in a square, landscape, or portrait frame.
3. Adjust the image with an Edit prompt until it looks right.
4. Generate the 3D model, then preview it and [export](https://hydrilla.ai/features#exports).

Every model comes back UV-unwrapped, with PBR maps, [details](https://hydrilla.ai/bluefox).

### Write prompts that say how the asset will be used

Be specific about scale and use. Naming the use, scale, and camera distance gives BlueFox a clearer brief.

| Prompt | Why it works |
|---|---|
| Low-poly wooden crate for a Unity mobile game | Names the style and engine |
| Weathered brass ship lantern with worn edges | Sets the material and detail level |
| Walnut lounge chair at real scale, for interior renders | Gives scale and use |
| Cargo container for a background set | Says it sits far from camera |

### Refine the image before you spend on 3D

Settle the look at the image stage, where a change is one more Edit prompt. Have a picture already? Use [image to 3D](https://hydrilla.ai/image-to-3d). [See what a model costs](https://hydrilla.ai/pricing)

---

URL: https://hydrilla.ai/image-to-3d

## Image to 3D: turn a picture into a 3D model

Upload a picture, and BlueFox, Hydrilla's 3D model, builds a segmented 3D model from it in Hydrilla AI, ready to preview and export.

### From picture to model in three steps

1. Upload a picture of the object you want.
2. Start the job, and the picture becomes a model split into parts. [Credits per job](https://hydrilla.ai/pricing)
3. Spin it in the preview, check each part, then [export](https://hydrilla.ai/features#exports).

### What BlueFox reads from your image

Image to 3D uses your reference to follow its silhouette, materials, and style. It works from what the camera captured, so sides the photo doesn't show are inferred. [How to shoot a good reference](https://hydrilla.ai/blog/reference-images)

---

URL: https://hydrilla.ai/water

## Water Agent, the AI 3D agent for artists and studios

Hydrilla Water Agent is the AI 3D agent that works alongside artists and studios, from brief to finished assets, inside the tools they already use.

Brief it as you would brief your team: the look, the pieces, the scene. It plans the set, builds it, and revises with you until it's right.

### Direct the set, piece by piece

- **Turn a brief into a plan.** Describe what the scene needs, and Water Agent plans the set with you before it builds.
- **Direct the look.** Set the style in your brief, and keep refining it in the same conversation.
- **Revise piece by piece.** Ask for a taller lantern or a darker crate, and the rest of the set stays as it is.
- **Work inside your tools.** Brief and revise from your engine or DCC, and each piece lands in the project you have open.

### From brief to finished set

1. Write the brief like a creative director: the pieces, the style, and where the assets will be used.
2. Review the plan and adjust it until it matches your intent.
3. Water Agent builds the set to the direction you gave it.
4. Check each piece, ask for changes in the conversation, and take the finished set into your project.

### Where Water Agent works

Water Agent works in the Hydrilla app, and inside Blender, Unity, Unreal, and Godot through the Hydrilla plugin. [Set up the plugin](https://hydrilla.ai/integrations)

### Questions about Water Agent

**What does Water Agent cost?**
Water Agent costs no credits and is included on every plan.

**Who is it for?**
3D artists, art leads, and studio teams who brief whole sets of assets and need them to hold together.

**Can a brief be a single asset?**
Yes. A brief can be one prop or a whole scene, and Water Agent plans only what you ask for.

**When should I use text to 3D instead?**
When you already know the one model you want. [Text to 3D](https://hydrilla.ai/text-to-3d) starts from a prompt, and [image to 3D](https://hydrilla.ai/image-to-3d) starts from a reference.

**How is Water Agent different from the MCP server?**
Water Agent is the agent inside Hydrilla. The MCP server lets your own AI agent drive Hydrilla from outside. [MCP server](https://hydrilla.ai/integrations/mcp)

### Bring your next brief

Open Water Agent with the brief for your next set.

---

URL: https://hydrilla.ai/features

## Generate, check, and export 3D with BlueFox

Generate from text or an image with BlueFox, Hydrilla's 3D model, check the result in the browser, and export it to your engine or DCC.

### Start from a prompt, an image, or a conversation

Describe the asset with [text to 3D](https://hydrilla.ai/text-to-3d), or upload a picture with [image to 3D](https://hydrilla.ai/image-to-3d). BlueFox builds either one.

#### Water Agent

Give Water Agent the brief for a whole set, and work through it piece by piece in one conversation, as you would with your art team. [How Water Agent works](https://hydrilla.ai/water)

### Check every model before you export

Orbit it, select parts, and check materials under light. Each result is a segmented mesh with UVs and PBR maps, [explained here](https://hydrilla.ai/bluefox).

### Export to the format your tool opens

Hydrilla exports GLB, FBX, OBJ, and USDZ, on every plan, Free included.

| Format | Use |
|---|---|
| GLB | Web viewers and real-time engines |
| FBX | DCC tools and engines that expect FBX |
| OBJ | Plain geometry between modeling tools |
| USDZ | AR viewers on iPhone and iPad |

### Send it straight into your tools

Engine and DCC plugins take models over the local Bridge, agents use MCP, and code calls the [REST API](https://hydrilla.ai/api). [All integrations](https://hydrilla.ai/integrations)

New models will be available through Water Agent as they arrive.

---

URL: https://hydrilla.ai/bluefox

## BlueFox

BlueFox, Hydrilla's 3D model, turns a prompt or a picture into a segmented 3D model with UVs and PBR textures. It's built by Hydrilla AI. Begin with a [typed prompt](https://hydrilla.ai/text-to-3d) or an [uploaded picture](https://hydrilla.ai/image-to-3d).

Current version BlueFox 1, generally available to everyone in Hydrilla.

### Ready for your pipeline from the first export

BlueFox is made for the many props, set pieces, and visualization assets a studio needs, and it delivers them in a shape your tools already read.

#### UVs and textures included
Every model arrives unwrapped, with PBR maps already attached, so it reacts to your scene's lights straight away.
#### Parts split for you
Handles, lids, and panels come back as separate pieces you can select, hide, or rework, with no fused mesh to cut apart first.
#### Works with your tools
Every Hydrilla plugin works with it, in your engine or DCC. [Integrations](https://hydrilla.ai/integrations)
#### No training on your data
Your prompts, pictures, and models stay out of our training sets. [How we handle data](https://hydrilla.ai/security)

### Parts, UVs, and PBR textures

BlueFox returns a mesh split into parts, with UVs and PBR texture maps. Select one part in Studio and leave the rest alone, or repaint the maps in your own tools.

### BlueFox at a glance

| Spec | BlueFox 1 |
|---|---|
| Version | BlueFox 1 |
| Availability | Generally available to everyone in Hydrilla |
| Inputs | Typed prompt or uploaded image |
| Output | Mesh in parts, UV-unwrapped, with PBR maps |
| Exports | [Hydrilla's export formats](https://hydrilla.ai/features#exports) |

### Where BlueFox fits, and where it stops

Use it for props, environment pieces, and visualization assets an artist will finish. BlueFox isn't built for CAD, manufacturing drawings, or finished hero assets that skip an artist pass. The full [model card](https://hydrilla.ai/research#model-card) lists intended use and inputs.

---

URL: https://hydrilla.ai/integrations

## Integrations

Hydrilla AI connects to the tools you already run: a Blender add-on, plugins for Unity, Unreal, and Godot, a local Bridge from Studio, and MCP and REST for custom pipelines.

### From Studio to your open scene

The local Bridge runs on your machine and sends meshes from Studio into Blender, Unity, Unreal, or Godot. Start it from a plugin, then use Send to DCC in Studio.

#### [Blender](https://hydrilla.ai/integrations/blender)
Generation in a sidebar tab, plus Studio sends.
#### [Unity](https://hydrilla.ai/integrations/unity)
Generation and GLB import inside the Unity Editor.
#### [Unreal Engine](https://hydrilla.ai/integrations/unreal)
A Python editor plugin for generation and import.
#### [Godot](https://hydrilla.ai/integrations/godot)
A Godot 4 editor dock that generates and receives.
#### [MCP server](https://hydrilla.ai/integrations/mcp)
Hydrilla generation for any MCP client.
#### [REST API](https://hydrilla.ai/api)
Generation jobs from your own code.

### What each integration does

| Tool | Generate in the tool | Receive from Studio | Sign-in |
|---|---|---|---|
| Blender | Yes | Bridge | API key |
| Maya | Yes | Bridge | API key |
| 3ds Max | Yes | Bridge | API key |
| Unity | Yes | Bridge | API key |
| Unreal Engine | Yes | Bridge | API key |
| Godot 4 | Yes | Bridge | API key |
| MCP server | Through your agent | No | API key |
| REST API | From your code | No | API key |

Sign-in (anchor #sign-in): The Blender add-on can use your Studio sign-in in the browser. Every plugin, and the MCP server, also accepts a hyd_live_ API key.

---

URL: https://hydrilla.ai/integrations/blender

## Hydrilla for Blender

The Hydrilla add-on for Blender generates from a prompt or image inside your scene. It also receives models that you send from Studio through the local Bridge.

Available | Hydrilla Team

### Install from disk

1. Download hydrilla-blender.zip using the button on this page.
2. In Blender, open Edit > Preferences > Add-ons.
3. Open the menu at the top right and choose Install from Disk.
4. Select hydrilla-blender.zip, then tick the box to enable the Hydrilla add-on.
5. In the 3D Viewport, press N to open the sidebar, then click the Hydrilla tab.

### Generate in the Hydrilla tab

Paste your API key once, then generate from a typed prompt or a picture. Click Run Bridge to receive models from Send to DCC in Studio or from your AI agent.

### Troubleshooting

**The add-on says my key was not accepted.**
Create a new key under API keys, paste it into the Hydrilla tab, and choose Check. The add-on uses an API key, so there is no browser sign-in to keep open.

**Nothing arrives when I send from Studio.**
Check that Run Bridge is active in the Hydrilla panel and Blender is open on a scene, then send again. Formats other than GLB are covered on [exports](https://hydrilla.ai/features#exports).

---

URL: https://hydrilla.ai/integrations/unity

## Hydrilla for Unity

Generate and import 3D models without leaving the Unity Editor. The plugin adds an Editor window that generates with your API key, and it accepts Studio sends over the Bridge whenever the project is open.

Available | Hydrilla Team

### Install

1. Download hydrilla-unity.zip from this page and unzip it.
2. Copy the Hydrilla folder into your project's Assets folder.
3. In the menu bar, open Window > Hydrilla.
4. Paste your API key, or click Run Bridge to receive models.

### Generate from the editor

Type a prompt or choose an image in the Hydrilla window and generate. Finished models download as GLB into Assets/Hydrilla, ready to drag into a scene.

### Check the import

Scale looks off? Check the [units table](https://hydrilla.ai/docs#scale). Axis or materials? Work through the [import checklist](https://hydrilla.ai/blog/import-ai-meshes).

---

URL: https://hydrilla.ai/integrations/unreal

## Hydrilla for Unreal Engine

Generate 3D models and bring them into Unreal Editor. A Python editor plugin runs generation from inside the editor, and it receives models you send from Studio over the Bridge.

Available | Hydrilla Team

### Install

1. Enable the Python Editor Script Plugin in Unreal, then restart the editor.
2. Unzip the download and place its Hydrilla folder in Content/Python or Plugins.
3. Open the Hydrilla menu in the editor's main menu bar.
4. Set your API key once from the Python console, then choose Run Bridge to receive models.

### Generate from the editor

Run a job from the editor's Python console with your own brief. GLB files land in Content/Hydrilla, where the glTF importer turns them into assets you can place, light, and test.

### Check the import

Check scale with the [units table](https://hydrilla.ai/docs#scale), and axis and materials with the [import guide](https://hydrilla.ai/blog/import-ai-meshes).

---

URL: https://hydrilla.ai/integrations/godot

## Hydrilla for Godot 4

Bring Hydrilla GLB into Godot 4 projects. The editor plugin generates through the API with your key and listens on the Bridge for models sent from Studio, so both routes end in the same folder.

Available | Hydrilla Team

### Install

1. Download the plugin and copy addons/hydrilla into your Godot project.
2. Open Project Settings > Plugins and enable the Hydrilla plugin.
3. Open the Hydrilla dock and paste your API key.
4. Generate from the dock, or click Run Bridge to receive models from Studio or your AI agent.

### Where models land

Imported meshes land under res://hydrilla/, so every generated asset sits in one folder you can move or version. For scale, see the [units table](https://hydrilla.ai/docs#scale); for axis and materials, the [import guide](https://hydrilla.ai/blog/import-ai-meshes).

---

URL: https://hydrilla.ai/integrations/mcp

## Hydrilla MCP server

Let AI agents generate 3D through Hydrilla over MCP. Hydrilla's MCP server calls the [REST API](https://hydrilla.ai/api) on an agent's behalf, running locally over stdio for Cursor, Claude Code, and other MCP clients. Your agent describes the asset, and the server handles the job from submission to the finished files.

### Install

1. Install Node.js 20 or newer. The server is the npm package hydrilla-mcp, started with npx -y hydrilla-mcp@latest.
2. Add your API key in a Hydrilla plugin, or set HYDRILLA_API_KEY in the server's MCP config. Never paste it into the chat.
3. Register the server in your MCP client with the command on this page, then restart the client.

the MCP server works on every plan, and generating a model uses your credits. [Plans](https://hydrilla.ai/pricing) Want an agent inside Hydrilla instead? [See Water Agent](https://hydrilla.ai/water)

---

URL: https://hydrilla.ai/api

## Hydrilla REST API

Run BlueFox, Hydrilla's 3D model, from your own code. The REST API uses the same AI 3D generation as the Hydrilla AI workspace, for asset pipelines, engines, and internal tools.

### Submit, poll, download

Submit a job, poll its status, then download the mesh and maps. Each job moves from queued to processing and ends completed or failed, so your pipeline can retry.

### What you can send and get back

**You send**
- A text prompt describing the asset and its use
- Or a reference image to follow
- Your API key with every request

**You get back**
- A job ID and its current status
- A mesh in parts, with UVs and texture maps
- Files in any of Hydrilla's [export formats](https://hydrilla.ai/features#exports)

### Access and authentication

Create a key in your account; keep it server-side. Plan access is on [pricing](https://hydrilla.ai/pricing), and volume through [Enterprise](https://hydrilla.ai/enterprise). Building for an AI agent? Use the [MCP server](https://hydrilla.ai/integrations/mcp).

### Pricing questions

**What does a model cost?**
A model from text costs 45 credits and a model from an uploaded image costs 30, at default quality.

**Do unused credits carry over?**
No. Allowances reset each billing month.

**How does the 14-day trial work?**
Start on the Free plan, or try any Monthly or Hourly plan, Pro included, free for 14 days. The trial needs a card.

**How do Hourly plans save?**
Hourly Pro gives Pro's 3,000 credits for 33% less, $8 instead of $12, in a chosen daily window. Hourly gives Starter's 900 credits for $3 instead of $5, in one chosen hour a day.

**Which plan includes the API?**
Pro includes REST API access. [API](https://hydrilla.ai/api)

### Start with the Free plan

Need more than Pro? [Enterprise](https://hydrilla.ai/enterprise)

Level dressing and prop sets for your game engine.

## 3D props and environment fill for game teams

Hydrilla AI gives game teams props and environment pieces for your game engine, generated with BlueFox, Hydrilla's 3D model, from typed briefs or uploaded pictures.

### From greybox to a filled level

Swap greybox blocks for generated crates, barrels, and debris while the layout is still changing, then keep the pieces that work. Working from a full level brief? [See Water Agent](https://hydrilla.ai/water)

### What you still do

- Retopology wherever the polygon budget is tight
- LODs for anything seen from several distances
- Collision shapes for anything the player touches
- A material check under your engine's own lighting and post-processing

### Straight into your engine

The [Unity](https://hydrilla.ai/integrations/unity), [Unreal Engine](https://hydrilla.ai/integrations/unreal), and [Godot](https://hydrilla.ai/integrations/godot) plugins put generated models into your project. Review scale and pivots before you build on them. Importing by hand? Use the [import guide](https://hydrilla.ai/blog/import-ai-meshes).

Fill the level now, and polish the pieces players will notice.

---

URL: https://hydrilla.ai/solutions/film

## 3D props and sets for previs and layout

Props and environments for animation and VFX often start as stand-ins. Hydrilla AI fills previs and layout scenes with set pieces generated from a [written prompt](https://hydrilla.ai/text-to-3d) or a still.

### Where generated assets fit

#### Previs
Block a sequence with generated props, so camera and timing work starts early. Bring them in through [Blender](https://hydrilla.ai/integrations/blender) or [Unreal Engine](https://hydrilla.ai/integrations/unreal).
#### Background set dressing
Fill shelves, streets, and rooms far from camera, where silhouette and material read count more than fine detail.
#### Lookdev bases
Begin a material study from a generated model and its PBR maps, then hand it to an artist to refine.

### Background first, hero by hand

Assets close to camera still need an artist's pass. Use generated models as a starting point for hero work, and check [the limits of BlueFox, Hydrilla's 3D model](https://hydrilla.ai/bluefox#limits).

Generate what the camera passes by, and save artist hours for what it lingers on.

---

URL: https://hydrilla.ai/solutions/architecture

## 3D furniture and fixtures for visualization

Furnish rooms for presentations and design reviews with furniture and fixtures generated in Hydrilla AI from a [photo](https://hydrilla.ai/image-to-3d) or a prompt.

### Good fits and poor fits

| Fit | Example |
|---|---|
| Good fit | Generic chairs, lamps, plants, and decor that fill a room |
| Good fit | Placeholder furnishings for an early design review |
| Poor fit | An exact catalogue piece the client intends to buy |
| Poor fit | Fixtures that need manufacturer dimensions ([limits](https://hydrilla.ai/bluefox#limits)) |

### Into your visualization tool

Check scale on import with the [units table](https://hydrilla.ai/docs#scale). Use the [Blender add-on](https://hydrilla.ai/integrations/blender), or pick the [format](https://hydrilla.ai/features#exports) your renderer prefers. Look over the PBR maps under your scene lighting before the review, since materials read differently in every renderer.

Dress the room with generated pieces, and keep the specified products exact.

---

URL: https://hydrilla.ai/solutions/xr

## 3D assets for AR, VR, and spatial apps

VR, AR, and spatial apps need many small, believable objects. BlueFox, Hydrilla's 3D model, generates them in Hydrilla AI, so you can check each against a headset's limits.

### Check the headset budget

Standalone headsets have tight limits on triangles, draw calls, and texture memory. Measure each asset against your target before it ships, and reduce or bake anything that exceeds it.

- Triangle count per asset
- Texture resolution per map
- Draw calls per material
- Collision and grab volumes for objects users can pick up

### Check it before the headset build

Preview each object in the browser first, then route headset builds through the [Unity](https://hydrilla.ai/integrations/unity) or [Unreal](https://hydrilla.ai/integrations/unreal) plugin. [Which file suits each platform](https://hydrilla.ai/features#exports)

Prototype the space with generated objects, then budget each one for the headset.

---

## 3D product models from product photos

### Enterprise questions, answered

**What is Hydrilla Enterprise?**
Hydrilla Enterprise gives studios a shared AI 3D workspace, [BlueFox](https://hydrilla.ai/bluefox), [Water Agent](https://hydrilla.ai/water), native 3D software plugins, an [MCP server](https://hydrilla.ai/integrations/mcp), and [REST API](https://hydrilla.ai/api) concurrency under one studio agreement with custom credit pools and pipeline support.

**What's the difference between Pro and Enterprise?**
Pro is a self-serve monthly plan for individuals and small teams: $12 a month for 3,000 credits, with REST API access. Enterprise is an agreement shaped around your studio, with seats in a shared workspace, API concurrency sized to your volume, custom credit pools, queue priority, and help connecting your pipeline. [See self-serve plans](https://hydrilla.ai/pricing).

**Which 3D software and AI agent workflows does Enterprise support?**
[Water Agent](https://hydrilla.ai/water) works inside the Hydrilla Studio workspace and directly inside Blender, Unity, Unreal Engine, and Godot 4 through [Hydrilla plugins](https://hydrilla.ai/integrations) and the local Bridge. Coding agents and internal studio automation connect through the [MCP server](https://hydrilla.ai/integrations/mcp) and the [REST API](https://hydrilla.ai/api).

**How does Water Agent work for studio teams?**
Water Agent is Hydrilla's AI 3D agent. Artists and leads brief an entire set of props or environment pieces in plain language, review the plan first, and revise individual pieces in conversation inside Studio or their 3D tool. Water Agent uses zero credits on every plan.

**What drives Enterprise pricing and credit pools?**
Enterprise is quoted around your studio's seats, API concurrency, monthly generation volume, and queue priority. Instead of separate individual caps, your team draws from one shared credit pool sized to your pipeline. On public plans, a default model costs 45 credits from text or 30 from an image.

**Who owns what we generate, and do you train on our data?**
You keep all rights in what you upload. As between you and Hydrilla AI, and to the extent the law allows, you own the 3D assets generated for you and may use them commercially. The [ownership section of the Terms](https://hydrilla.ai/terms#ownership) has the exact wording. Prompts, reference images, and generated models are never used to train our models, on any plan. [Read security details](https://hydrilla.ai/security).

**Can we sign our own agreement or run a vendor security review?**
Yes. Enterprise runs on an agreement shaped around your studio. Send your legal requirements or security questionnaire to founders@hydrilla.ai, naming your studio and timeline, and we will respond in writing with what we can confirm.

**Can we evaluate on Pro before moving to Enterprise?**
Yes. Your team can test [BlueFox](https://hydrilla.ai/bluefox), [Water Agent](https://hydrilla.ai/water), and the [plugins](https://hydrilla.ai/integrations) on any self-serve plan first. When you are ready for shared seats, custom credit pools, or higher API concurrency, contact our team and we will structure Enterprise around your current setup.

## Get started with Hydrilla

This guide takes a new Hydrilla AI account to its first AI 3D export, step by step, in the browser.

### Your first export

1. Sign up, then open Studio.
2. Create a workspace so a project's generations stay together.
3. Generate: write a prompt in [text to 3D](https://hydrilla.ai/text-to-3d), or drop a photo into [image to 3D](https://hydrilla.ai/image-to-3d).
4. Preview the model: orbit it and check parts and materials.
5. Choose a format in the export menu and export.
6. Import the file into Blender, Unity, Unreal, or Godot, or send it with a [plugin](https://hydrilla.ai/integrations).

### Preview and export

The preview shows the model under light, so shape and material problems appear before you download. The export menu lists every format; [which suits which tool](https://hydrilla.ai/features#exports).

### Workspaces and credits

A workspace keeps a project's generations and versions in one place. Each generation spends plan credits, and your account shows what is left. [Cost per model](https://hydrilla.ai/pricing)

### Get the scale right on import

Every tool assumes its own unit and up axis. A mesh in meters arrives a hundred times too small in a tool expecting centimeters, unless the importer converts it.

| Tool | Unit | Up axis | What to watch |
|---|---|---|---|
| Blender | Meters | Z up | Apply scale before you export again |
| Unreal Engine | Centimeters | Z up | Check the import scale field |
| Unity | Meters | Y up | Compare against a default cube |
| glTF 2.0 (GLB) | Meters | Y up | Importers read this as the source |
| Godot 4 | Meters | Y up | Compare against a one-meter box |

### Water Agent

Open Water Agent in the Hydrilla app, or through the Hydrilla plugin inside Blender, Unity, Unreal, or Godot. Describe your brief, review the plan, and revise piece by piece until the set is right. [What Water Agent does](https://hydrilla.ai/water)

Running jobs from code? See the [REST API](https://hydrilla.ai/api). Account questions are in the [FAQ](https://hydrilla.ai/faq).

## What makes a good reference image for image to 3D?

publish date | Hydrilla Team

A good reference shows one subject, whole and in focus, against a plain background in soft, even light, from a slight angle rather than flat on. The clearer its outline, the less guessing [image to 3D](https://hydrilla.ai/image-to-3d) in Hydrilla AI does.

### Subject, framing, and light

Let the object fill most of the frame, with a small margin on every side. A three-quarter angle shows two faces and a sense of depth. Avoid hard shadows and strong reflections, which can read as shape. A sharp phone photo is enough.

Good example caption: One chair, three-quarter view, plain wall, soft daylight, nothing cropped.
Poor example caption: The same chair cut off at the legs, in a busy room, under hard window light.

### The sides the camera can't see

A single image can't show the back of an object, so the model has to infer it. When the hidden side matters, pick the angle that shows the faces you care about most.

### Before you upload

- One subject, with nothing touching it
- Sharp at full size, without blur or heavy compression
- The whole object in frame, with every edge visible
- A plain background that contrasts with the subject
- Even light, without blown highlights or colored casts

---

URL: https://hydrilla.ai/blog/import-ai-meshes

## How do you import an AI-generated mesh into a game engine?

publish date | Hydrilla Team

[Export a GLB or FBX](https://hydrilla.ai/features#exports), then check the up axis and materials on import. Most problems come from tools disagreeing about orientation and texture setup, not from the mesh itself.

### Why does the model arrive on its side?

Tools disagree on the up axis: Blender and Unreal use Z up, while Unity, Godot, and glTF use Y up, so a model can arrive lying on its side. Units and scale are covered in the [docs](https://hydrilla.ai/docs#scale).

### How do you keep the materials?

GLB packs its textures inside the file, so materials usually arrive assigned. Other formats often point to separate texture files, so keep the maps beside the mesh and check the UVs came through. Base color is sRGB; roughness, metalness, and normal maps are linear.

### Import checklist

1. Pick the format your importer prefers: GLB or FBX.
2. Fix the up axis in import settings, not by rotating the object.
3. Open each material and confirm every texture slot has a map.
4. If bumps look inverted, flip the normal map's green channel (Unreal uses DirectX style).
5. Save the import settings as a preset, so every later asset arrives the same way.

### Prefer a plugin?

Plugins for the three engines, [Unity](https://hydrilla.ai/integrations/unity), [Unreal Engine](https://hydrilla.ai/integrations/unreal), and [Godot](https://hydrilla.ai/integrations/godot), place GLB files in a fixed project folder for you.

## How do you choose an AI 3D generator?

Start from the job, not the demo reel. Decide what the asset has to do in your engine or DCC, then test each tool against ten practical criteria and one shared brief in your own scene.

### Ten criteria that decide fit

| Criterion | Why it matters | How to check |
|---|---|---|
| Inputs | Text, one image, or several views change how much you can direct | Run the same prompt and photo in each tool |
| Output type | A mesh, a point cloud, and a splat need different pipelines | Open the file and see what is inside |
| Parts | Separate parts make material and edit work simpler | Count the objects after import |
| PBR maps | The maps decide how an asset reacts to your lighting | List the texture maps that come with the file |
| Formats | The file has to open where your team works | Export every format you need and import each one |
| Engine and DCC path | Plugins and bridges remove manual import steps | Install the plugin and send one asset across |
| API | Pipelines and internal tools need jobs run from code | Read the API reference and run a single job |
| Licensing | Commercial use and ownership can differ by plan | Check the license wording for the plan you would buy |
| Data and security | Studios need to know where inputs and outputs go | Ask for the security page and data-use terms |
| Cost predictability | Published credit math sets the real cost per asset | Work out the cost of one finished model |

### Run a fair bake-off

Test any AI 3D generator on the same brief, in your own engine or DCC, before you commit. Keep the brief short and the scoring sheet fixed, so the comparison stays about the output and not the presentation.

1. Write one brief with three assets taken from a real task.
2. Generate each asset in every tool with identical inputs.
3. Import the results into your scene, under your own lighting.
4. Score each criterion, then log the cleanup time per asset.

### Where Hydrilla fits

Hydrilla AI runs BlueFox, Hydrilla's 3D model, which returns segmented meshes with PBR maps from a prompt or an image. Its [fit and limits](https://hydrilla.ai/bluefox#limits) are stated on the model page. Its [model](https://hydrilla.ai/bluefox), [exports](https://hydrilla.ai/features#exports), [security](https://hydrilla.ai/security), and [credit costs](https://hydrilla.ai/pricing) are all public.

Checked 24 Oct 2026

## About Hydrilla

Hydrilla AI is an AI 3D workspace for studio and artist pipelines. We build the Hydrilla workspace and BlueFox, Hydrilla's 3D model. Despite the name, we're a software company, not the aquatic plant.

### One company, its research lab, and its model

Hydrilla AI is the product and company; Hawan Research Labs is its research lab. The lab builds BlueFox. Read about [Hawan Research Labs](https://hydrilla.ai/research), the [model](https://hydrilla.ai/bluefox), and the [workspace](https://hydrilla.ai/features).

### Company facts

| Fact | Detail |
|---|---|
| Company | Hydrilla AI |
| Founders | Tharak Nagaveti, Dharani Kumar, and Tejesh Varma |
| Availability | Worldwide, including the United States, India, Japan, China, and France (web workspace, plugins, MCP server, and REST API) |

Want to see who builds Hydrilla, or work with us? Meet the [team](https://hydrilla.ai/team), or see how we [hire](https://hydrilla.ai/careers).

URL: https://hydrilla.ai/research

## Research

Hawan Research Labs is Hydrilla AI's research lab. It's where we build BlueFox, Hydrilla's 3D model. Below is the model card. [About Hydrilla](https://hydrilla.ai/about)

### What we work on

Generating 3D from text and images: meshes split into usable parts, physically based materials, and assets that hold up in game, film, architecture, and XR scenes. [Meet the team](https://hydrilla.ai/team)

### BlueFox 1 model card

The card lists what the current model takes in, what it returns, and what it's for.

| Field | Detail |
|---|---|
| Model | BlueFox 1, in the BlueFox family |
| Built by | Hawan Research Labs, the research lab of Hydrilla AI |
| Availability | Generally available to everyone in Hydrilla |
| Inputs | Text prompt, reference image |
| Outputs | Segmented mesh with UVs and textures (PBR maps) |
| Exports | [Hydrilla's export formats](https://hydrilla.ai/features#exports) |
| Intended use | Props, environments, visualization, and starting assets for an artist pass |
| Not intended for | CAD or precision engineering |
| Training data | Customer data isn't used ([security](https://hydrilla.ai/security)) |
| Repository | [Hugging Face](https://huggingface.co/Hydrilla/BlueFox3D) |

## Careers at Hydrilla

Hydrilla AI is a small team building an AI 3D workspace for artists and studios: meshes, materials, exports, and the software around them.

### Who we hire

| Team | What you work on |
|---|---|
| Engineering | Full-stack product, 3D runtime, and generation infrastructure. |
| 3D and research | Model quality, mesh structure, materials, and evaluation for BlueFox, Hydrilla's 3D model. |

### How to apply

Email founders@hydrilla.ai with the subject "Careers / your name", links to your work, and your location, even if no role fits yet. Meet the [team](https://hydrilla.ai/team) or read [about Hydrilla](https://hydrilla.ai/about) first.

## Contact Hydrilla

Reach the team behind Hydrilla AI about your account, a generation, or press. Pick the route that fits.

### Choose a route

| Route | How |
|---|---|
| Support | Account, billing, or a generation that went wrong: email founders@hydrilla.ai, or check the [FAQ](https://hydrilla.ai/faq) and [docs](https://hydrilla.ai/docs) first. |
| Press | Interviews and logos: write to founders@hydrilla.ai with your outlet and deadline. |
| Sales and demos | Seats, volume, or a walkthrough live on [Enterprise](https://hydrilla.ai/enterprise). |

### Send a message

Replies come from founders@hydrilla.ai.

## How Hydrilla protects your studio assets

Hydrilla AI protects the keys to your account, keeps your work inside your AI 3D workspace, and hands files to your pipeline.

Oct 1, 2026 | Hydrilla Team

### Your data doesn't train our models

We don't use your data to train our models. That holds for every account on every plan, including your prompts, the reference images you upload, and the models you generate.

### Accounts and stored assets

Sign-in runs through Clerk, and each session belongs to one user. Generated meshes stay scoped to your workspace. Your data is stored securely, and reaching it takes a signed-in account.

- Signed-in pages are kept out of search engines
- API keys are created and managed from your account

### Exports and vendor reviews

Once you download an export, the file lives in your own pipeline. For a questionnaire or vendor review, use Contact security below, or [talk to our team](https://cal.com/hydrilla). See also the [Privacy Policy](https://hydrilla.ai/privacy) and [Terms](https://hydrilla.ai/terms).
